hints: Each heap is an independent game where a move removes 1, 2, or 3 sticks.
For one heap, losing sizes repeat every four: sizes divisible by 4 are losing.
Replace each heap by its remainder modulo 4 and XOR the remainders.
analogy: A heap's strategic size is its remainder after removing groups of four.
example: A single heap of 4 is losing because every move leaves 1, 2, or 3 sticks, all winning positions.
algorithm: For each test case, XOR x_i mod 4 across all heaps. Print first if the XOR is nonzero and second otherwise.
correctness: A single heap has Grundy value x mod 4 because each move can reach the preceding one, two, or three residues. Independent heaps combine by XOR, so zero is losing and nonzero is winning.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space per test case.
